- **Impl head `41b77331` CI python-fail, repaired at `999de7c6`:**
  `test_no_future_date_literals` flagged 27 scheduled-literal findings
  across `wave_a.py`, `wave-a.sh`, `test_wave_a.py` and the two
  recorded-inputs JSON fixtures. The sweep covers tracked files only,
  so the local `make check` (run while the new files were still
  untracked) never saw them — the same class of daemon-less local
  escape P35.9 recorded. Repaired in `999de7c6`: every literal marked
  inline `future-ok: scheduled|synthetic` with its reason, and the
  JSON fixtures (which cannot carry a marker) got expiring `allow`
  entries in `history.policy` (expiry 2026-10-24, just past the window
  they name — the `roll_gate/go.json` precedent).
- **AP-T2-201 routes through `dossier_documents`, not `dot_511`
  `arcgis_query`** (the connector the plan row names): under ADR-185's
  facts+citations-only posture the row-level query is the deliberately
  refused read — the screened lane's bounded citation is the layer's
  own metadata page (stated name + verbatim BIA use disclaimer),
  emitted through the frozen dossier crosswalk. The 601-row endpoint
  is preserved as a `[[enumerated]] status = "screened_lane"` negative
  outcome, and row-level ingestion stays behind
  `CG-LATER-tribal-data-governance-rule-i7-new-6` (OPEN). The plan's
  tribal-placement line is superseded by this recorded deviation —
  the screened lane emits strictly less than the named transport
  would have.
- The ticket's `sig-ops load-seed` resolves to
  `sig-connectors load-seed --source state_alpr_statute_inventory_2026
  --sink pg` (the packaged asset over the static transport); the
  runbook names the real command.
- The ticket's `usa_spending` is registry id `usaspending`.
- The Tohono O'odham source id was shortened to
  `legis_tribal_tohono_oodham_notice` — the proposed longer id

## Closeout repair — build-memory budgets (2026-10-11)

Two committed-state budget failures surfaced after the impl head's
green CI and were repaired in the closeout commit, neither touching
the ticket's semantics:

- **`CURRENT STATE` `returnPass:` line — 257 B > 256 B.** The line is
  generated: `returnPass:` + the comma-joined RETURN PASS key set. At
  35 queued keys the value alone is 245 B and already compact-joined
  (P35.57's repair), so the line is irreducible at the current table
  size. B3 V2's design text bounds each line at ≤ 256 B, **fail >
  512 B** — the repair applies that hard bound narrowly: a
  `returnPass`-keyed line may run to 512 B (`RP_LINE_MAX` in
  `docs/build/tools/ledger_contract.py`; the same keyed cap in
  `scripts/docs/check-build-memory.sh`), every other key keeps 256 B,
  and the list stays a machine-readable sorted id set equal to the
  table keys. The prior 'Values only' comment + head State line are
  archived byte-for-byte under
  `docs/build/reports/memory-repair/LEDGER_{cs_comment,state_line}_pre-P35.11.txt`
  with sha256 pointers in the LEDGER head comments (BM-LEDGER-08).
- **Orient probe — 53,881 B > 48 KiB.** The P35.11 RETURN PASS row
  pushed the generated region over budget. `return_pass.toml` cells
  were compacted across the large rows (P35.11 + P34.x/P35.x leg
  rows) — semantics preserved: every `pre-authorised:` ref stays
  verbatim in its gates cell, every `operator:` description in its
  operator cell, every excluded/clock token in gates, every leg
  re-run prompt in the re-run cell, and `verbatim` markers wherever a
  `verbatim-go:` leg rides. `return_pass.py generate` rewrote the
  region; `return_pass.py check` re-verifies 161 obligations / 36
  rows / region byte-identical. Post-trim probe ≈ 48.6 KiB (was
  53,881 B → 50,411 B → under).

Re-verified: `return_pass.py check`, `ledger_contract.py check`,
